goal: An autonomous trading research factory that continuously converts raw ideas into scored evidence across crypto, forex, and prediction markets.

plan.title: Test volatility regime ATR-based conviction filter on BTC - avoid low-conviction conditions
plan.objective: Test volatility_regime.py strategy with ATR-based conviction filter on BTC to validate whether explicitly avoiding low-volatility (low-conviction) periods improves robustness vs prior EMA Trend Gate results
plan.hypothesis: The volatility_regime.py ATR-based conviction filter (entering only during volatility expansion after contraction) will achieve >= 70% positive Sharpe windows and improved OOS Sharpe vs EMA Trend Gate baseline (61.1% positive windows, 0.664 OOS Sharpe on BNB), by explicitly avoiding low-conviction conditions that the EMA-only filter does not address
plan.strategy_rationale: The backlog item explicitly asks to avoid trading in low-conviction market conditions. The existing volatility_regime.py strategy implements exactly this: ATR% percentile detects contractions (low-conviction), only enters during expansions (high-conviction). This differs from EMA Trend Gate which filters by trend direction only, not conviction level. Prior EMA Trend Gate lessons show regime filters help (BTC 0.998 vs ETH 0.528 Sharpe), but this tests whether ATR-based conviction filtering is even more robust.
plan.instrument_selection_rule: Single asset: BTC/USDT - best performer with prior regime-filtered experiments (0.998 OOS Sharpe vs ETH 0.528)
plan.timeframe: 1h with 4h regime detection for volatility contraction/expansion
dataset_requirements: BTC/USDT 1h OHLCV from Binance, minimum 3 years history for robust WFA

historical_depth_requirement.justification: BTC deep dataset provides maximum realistic crypto history. Multi-year history required for reliable WFA. Short windows not justified as BTC is the most liquid crypto asset with deepest available history.

source_plan.selection_reason: BTC deep dataset already exists locally at workspace/data/binance_btcusdt_1h_deep.csv with ~64k rows of clean 1h data from 2018

plan.scope_selection_rationale: BTC is chosen because: (1) Prior EMA Trend Gate lessons show it performs best with regime filters (0.998 OOS Sharpe vs ETH 0.528), (2) Deepest available history for robust WFA, (3) Most liquid crypto asset providing cleanest signals. Testing whether ATR-based conviction filtering improves on the 61.1% positive window rate achieved by EMA direction-only filter.

data_acquisition.reason: binance_btcusdt_1h_deep.csv already exists with ~64k rows of clean 1h data

inputs: Strategy: volatility_regime.py (LightweightVolatilityRegime) - implements ATR-based contraction/expansion detection
Prior baseline: EMA Trend Gate on BNB achieved 61.1% positive windows with 0.664 OOS Sharpe
implementation_steps: 1. Update volatility_regime WFA config to use btcusdt_1h_deep.csv data source instead of btcusdt_1h_full.csv
2. Configure WFA with 3-month training, 1-month testing, 100 Optuna trials for parameter optimization
3. Run WFA to discover best ATR-based conviction filter parameters
4. Evaluate positive window rate vs 70% threshold and compare to EMA Trend Gate 61.1% baseline
5. Document whether explicit conviction filtering improves robustness

evaluation_criteria.status_gate: WFA completes with at least 30 windows and 200 total trades

fallback_if_blocked: If WFA fails on BTC, try ETHUSDT as alternative asset
If data unavailable, fetch fresh BTC 1h from Binance API
notes: This experiment directly tests the backlog item: add regime filter to avoid trading in low-conviction market conditions
volatility_regime.py implements ATR-based conviction filtering - enters only during volatility expansion after contraction
Comparison baseline: EMA Trend Gate on BNB achieved 61.1% positive windows, 0.664 OOS Sharpe - we target >= 70% positive windows
If ATR-based conviction filtering improves positive window rate, it validates the hypothesis that avoiding low-conviction conditions improves robustness
